120100101.text: We're looking for the Great Mujina Youkai!

120100102.text: Do you know where it lives?

120100104.text: Huh? You've never heard of it?

120100105.text: It's a sneaky monster that goes 'round playing tricks on people! It's got magic powers and can even shapeshift into anything it wants!

120100106.text: One time, the Great Mujina Youkai stole some rice from our house. And this other time, it pushed my dad into the river.

120100107.text: Sounds like a very naughty little monster!

120100108.text: Why are you out looking for it?

120100109.text: 'Cause, we've finally found out how to chase it away!

120100110.text: My dad said that the Great Mujina Youkai likes to play tricks on people who stay out all the time and don't come home when they're supposed to.

120100111.text: So all we need to do is chase it away, then we can come out and play whenever we want!

120100112.text: This monster sounds scary, though... Aren't you guys afraid?

120100113.text: Surely your parents must be worried about you?

120100114.text: Not really. I told my dad that I was going to find the Great Mujina Youkai with some friends, and he didn't even say anything.

120100115.text: So, we think it must be weak right now! It's probably hiding away so it can rest!

120100116.text: Yeah! So as long as we get home before it gets its strength back, we'll be safe.

120100117.text: Hmm, something sounds very strange about all of this... But Paimon can't say exactly what it is...

120100121.text: Yeah... Paimon feels like the Great Mujina Youkai is one of those storybook monsters that doesn't exist in the real world.

subQuests.subQuestName: Catch up to the children who are about to leave

120100201.text: #Cheer up guys, don't be so down. {F#She}{M#He} was only joking back there. How could the Great Mujina Youkai not exist, huh?

120100202.text: B—But, we've never seen it for ourselves...

120100203.text: That's because the Great Mujina Youkai is extra powerful! And that's exactly why I need your help, isn't it?

120100205.text: It's okay, don't be discouraged. Hey, remember, if you wanna be a hero, you gotta have patience — and wisdom, too.

120100206.text: Even if you can't find it right now, it'll definitely show up before the fireworks show starts. So remember to come and pick up your weapons from me before then, okay?

120100207.text: No matter how powerful the Great Mujina Youkai might be, it's no match for my specially made fireworks! Just light 'em up and you'll scare it off, no problem.

120100208.text: It's up to you guys to protect your homes, your crops, and your folks!

120100209.text: Got it! Thanks, Miss Yoimiya, we'll try and be more patient!

120100210.text: Oh yeah, hold up a sec. I have a few slips of paper for you guys — one each. Remember to give it to your parents and tell them to keep it safe.

120100211.text: Just tell them it's from Yoimiya. They'll know what it's about.

120100212.text: Okay! Thank you, Yoimiya! We're gonna go back now.

120100213.text: Thanks, Yoimiya! Come play with us soon!

120100214.text: Sure thing, will do! Take care on the way back, and I'll see you later!

120100218.text: Ah, so it WAS you guys. I guessed as much from the way the kids described you. No worries, though, I'm not blaming you.

120100219.text: The Great Mujina Youkai is pretty popular with the kids, so of course they're gonna get upset if someone tries to tell them it doesn't exist.

120100220.text: Okay... but it definitely doesn't exist... right?

120100221.text: Yeah, the first time I heard about it, I knew straight away that it was probably something the parents had come up with to stop the kids from running off all the time.

120100222.text: But when the kids asked me about it, I didn't wanna break it to them. I just told them that it looks cute, likes to play pranks, and doesn't hurt people.

120100223.text: So I guess now, the kids' impression of the Great Mujina Youkai is mostly influenced by me.

120100224.text: Huh... So in a way, this monster is all a product of your creativity...

120100225.text: Surely it's a bad idea to keep the lie going like that?

120100226.text: Maybe so. In any case, I'm not gonna be the one who exposes it.

120100227.text: Sure, it's likely that the parents just wanted to stop the kids from staying out all the time. But they could have easily had other reasons, too.

120100228.text: If I just go ahead and tell them that the Great Mujina Youkai doesn't exist without knowing the full story, then who knows — I may be doing more harm than good.

120100229.text: Besides, they're just kids. They should be allowed to believe it if it makes them happy. That's more important to them than questioning what's real and what isn't.

120100230.text: Heck, I entertain my fair share of fantasies too... The Fire Diamond that spins around and shoots out lights that are all the colors of the rainbow... Ooh — the Mist Spirits that live far off in the mountains and guide you to fairyland if you can find them...

120100231.text: I know that they don't really exist, but I still enjoy believing in them. If someone came up to me and starting telling me to "stop being so stupid, they don't exist, nyah nyah nyah"...

120100232.text: I'd give them the evil eyes and tell them to get the heck out of my face! Because... grr, it's just so annoying!

120100302.text: The fireworks show is almost upon us, and the fireworks for each family are almost ready.

120100303.text: Oh, new faces? Who are these two? Friends, or customers?

120100304.text: A bit of both, actually. They arrived in Inazuma just recently. Can't let them miss out on a fireworks show after coming all this way, can we?

120100305.text: Hahaha, well, either way, come on in and have a seat and I, Naganohara Ryuunosuke, will tell you all about the long history of the Naganoharas.

120100306.text: That can wait. Pops, I need to ask you about something.

120100308.text: *sigh* Pops has started telling his stories again...

120100309.text: Sorry about this — ever since Pops had his accident, his ears don't work too well.

120100310.text: Really? But for a moment there, it almost seemed like you were having a coherent conversation...

120100311.text: Much, much later, people eventually realized that if you grind certain minerals into dust, they burn with many beautiful colors.

120100314.text: Did they deliver those firework materials that we ordered yet?

120100315.text: Oh, yesterday's fireworks have all been delivered. So have the ones from the day before yesterday, and the ones from the day before that.

120100316.text: No, Pops. I meant the materials. The materials that we ordered. They should have arrived today.

120100317.text: Today's fireworks are almost ready, too, don't you worry! Hehe, your old man's skills are still as sharp as ever.

120100318.text: No— Pops, the materials! The raw materials for making fireworks.

120100323.text: Sorry, sorry... Paimon got all excited because you finally got the message across, hehe...

120100324.text: The materials aren't here yet. The couriers did come over to explain why, but... Well, I think they did, but I couldn't quite hear what they were saying...

120100325.text: No worries, as long as we know, that's fine. We can just make them later. Oh, uh — don't forget to take the goods in when they deliver them, okay, Pops?

120100326.text: Of course, leave it to me.

120100327.text: Oh, sorry if we were a little loud. It's always the way, though — it's like that every time I need to ask pops something.

120100329.text: Uh-huh, that's my pops! He's a good person, alright. Everyone around here respects him.

120100332.text: Because my pops is deaf, he never argues with anyone, and never contradicts them. He just listens cheerfully.

120100333.text: When I was little, I thought it was because he really understood me, and agreed with whatever I had to say. So, I'd tell my pops everything.

120100334.text: Eventually, I realized that the reason he was like that was that he's deaf. But I still tell him stories every day.

120100335.text: Huh? Why would you do that?

120100336.text: It just makes me happy to see him smile. And it keeps him from being lonely, right?

120100337.text: Anyway. More importantly right now, the fireworks show is right around the corner and the materials still haven't arrived. We need to think of an alternative...

120100339.text: Wah! Oh, you scared me there! I thought I told you to be more careful before you speak?

120100331.text: Hehe, I get told that a lot.

subQuests.subQuestName: Confirm the source of the sound

120100401.text: No one's looking. Okay, you can come out now. Uh, come around the side.

120100402.text: *sigh* We're lucky that no one from the Tenryou Commission was around, otherwise, we'd all be in big trouble.

120100403.text: Sorry, I guess I was a little rash. But when I heard you come back, I just...

120100404.text: Don't worry, Sakujirou. So far, at least, everything is going according to plan.

120100405.text: We're going to look for firework materials shortly. While we're out, we'll sort out the boat situation for you, as promised.

120100406.text: Thank you for all your help.

120100409.text: He's one of our old customers. He came back to Inazuma from the outside world not long ago. While he was smuggling himself in, the Tenryou Commission found him and put out a warrant for his arrest...

120100411.text: Shhhh, keep it down! We don't want to draw any unwanted attention.

120100412.text: If Sakujirou is caught, there's no knowing what crimes they could charge him with. All we can do is find him a boat and send him out of Inazuma again.

120100413.text: But isn't there a thunderstorm out in the ocean?

120100414.text: Yeah, we know it's going to be dangerous, but there aren't many other options left.

120100415.text: What if the boat capsizes? Uhh! Drowning is really scary!

120100416.text: If things are this bad, couldn't you have just not come back in the first place?

120100417.text: Well... There is something I felt I had to do...

120100418.text: But as soon as I got back, I started hearing about all these unbelievable changes. I had made my mind up, originally, but now I'm not sure anymore...

120100419.text: I didn't want to cause any trouble for Yoimiya or Mr. Ryuunosuke, but I'm very grateful to them for taking me in.

120100420.text: Hey, no worries, you're more than welcome. Remember what I said? As long as you've got that little piece of paper, you'll always be a valued customer of the Naganoharas.

120100501.text: Oh, don't worry about me, go take care of business first. There'll always be time for my stories later.

120100502.text: I have a lot of time, and a lot of stories to tell, too.

120109901.text: Inazuma is home to the Yae Publishing House, and a lot of people who like to write stories, too. In fact, most of what they write is based off of the kinds of fairy tales I was just talking about.

120109902.text: A bunch of them have bad endings, though. Like, oh — the Fire Diamond will get put in a rich person's gallery, where it will never be ignited again.

120109903.text: Or someone will see the Mist Spirit, and not manage to catch it, but because they angered it, it'll never show itself again.

120109904.text: The hero who slays the dragon becomes the next dragon... The sacred sword that once fought the darkness now becomes a doomsday weapon...

120109905.text: *sigh* I know these kinds of stories are all the rage nowadays, but... I really can't bring myself to like them.

120109906.text: If something's magical, it should be kept that way.

120109907.text: Oh yeah, if it's fine with you, can I ask how you two first met?

120109908.text: #{F#She}{M#He} saved me from drowning this one time, and after that, we started traveling together... Why do you ask?

120109909.text: Oh, nothing... I'm just quite envious of your relationship.

120109910.text: If my pops had a person like you around, his being deaf wouldn't hold things up all the time.

120109911.text: ...Huh? Why do you look so excited?

120109913.text: You said "person," and not "floating child," or "mascot"!
